.\artifacts\DIAGNOSIS.md:1:# Diagnosis: Adjacent Scatter Plot Overlay
.\artifacts\DIAGNOSIS.md:5:On the professional demo's `3D Explore` tab, the left plot is a `Scatter3D` and the smaller right plot is a `ScatterPlot2D`. `ScatterPlot2D` is not a separate renderer; it subclasses `Scatter3D` and uses the same native `scatter_3d` widget/runtime. When multiple scatter surfaces are visible, clicking/dragging outside the left plot or interacting with the neighboring plot can cause the cached/offscreen-rendered plot textures to composite into the same screen rectangle, visually combining/overlaying the two plots.
.\artifacts\DIAGNOSIS.md:7:The existing adjacent plot probe did not catch this because it checks stable data signatures and `active_scatter_id`, not whether the composited pixels land in the correct rectangle.
.\artifacts\DIAGNOSIS.md:13:- Professional demo route: `python tools/visual_audit.py --target all-features-professional-explore --sizes 1440x900`
.\artifacts\DIAGNOSIS.md:14:- Adjacent plot probe: `python tools/visual_audit.py --target adjacent-scatter-interaction --sizes 1120x720`
.\artifacts\DIAGNOSIS.md:30:- `examples/all_features_professional_demo.py:579-594` creates the large left `Scatter3D`.
.\artifacts\DIAGNOSIS.md:31:- `examples/all_features_professional_demo.py:605-612` creates the right `ScatterPlot2D`.
.\artifacts\DIAGNOSIS.md:32:- `python/dragongui/widgets.py:11752-11756` shows `ScatterPlot2D` subclasses `Scatter3D` and keeps `kind = Scatter3D.kind`, so both plots share the native scatter runtime.
.\artifacts\DIAGNOSIS.md:39:Because `queue.write_buffer` writes are queued before the command buffer is submitted, multiple writes to the same uniform buffer in one frame can be observed by later GPU execution as the final value, not as a per-draw snapshot. With two cached scatter widgets, both composite draws can therefore use the last scatter's `target_rect`. Since each draw still samples its own per-widget texture, the visible result is the left and right plot images being drawn into the same plot area.
.\artifacts\DIAGNOSIS.md:60:Any screen with two or more `Scatter3D`/`ScatterPlot2D` widgets can exhibit it when at least two visible scatters use the offscreen/composite path in the same frame. This includes:
.\artifacts\DIAGNOSIS.md:62:- Professional demo `3D Explore`
.\artifacts\DIAGNOSIS.md:64:- Any custom app with adjacent `Scatter3D` and/or `ScatterPlot2D`
.\artifacts\DIAGNOSIS.md:66:The line plot renderer is not the same issue: it renders inside the base pass and does not use this scatter compositor uniform.
.\artifacts\DIAGNOSIS.md:86:- Force both plots through the offscreen/composite path, e.g. set `interactive_render_scale < 1.0` or ensure cached full-scale compositing is active.
.\artifacts\DIAGNOSIS.md:88:- Assert the left and right plot rectangles retain distinct pixel signatures and do not both draw into the last scatter's rectangle.
.\artifacts\DIAGNOSIS.md:89:- Rebuild/reinstall the native library before running the professional demo, because the user's last complaint indicates they may have rerun against an old `_dragongui.pyd`.
